video_title: Amar’e Stoudemire On Getting Inducted Into the Hall of Fame, T-Mac, Knicks & 7SOL Suns

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter and Amar’e Stoudemire discuss Anthony Davis's contract extension
quotes.excerpt: Anthony Davis is giving the Wizards the trial period before he decides if he wants to sign

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: Anthony Davis is giving the Wizards the trial period before he decides if he wants to sign his extension. I thought this was interesting because at one point he said he's excited about what they've done and the talent that they brought in. I think he will be an asset to the team. I think they give him the veteran presence that they need. Do you agree with his approach and what are your thoughts about just that?

text_blocks.speaker: Amar’e Stoudemire
text_blocks.text: Yes, I have no problem with the approach. This is a team that has been trying to figure out how to draft and get players in free agency to build its team up. I think they have done a phenomenal job over the past couple years. Last year getting Trey Young, also drafting Trey Johnson, I like that draft pick, and bringing Anthony Davis over there and of course, AJ. So for me, yes, let's give them. I'm a vet, I've been in this league well over 12, 13 years. I want to see what direction they're heading in. So far it looks good, but for me, I need to make sure like this is a place I can contend for a championship because I'm on my way out.

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter and Amar’e Stoudemire on Anthony Davis's availability
quotes.excerpt: availability plays a huge factor in that too. He has to be available to say in the first 25 games

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: He told the team a trial period. He's in a trial period to see what it looks like and see where we go from there. But availability plays a huge factor in that too. He has to be available to say in the first 25 games.

text_blocks.speaker: Amar’e Stoudemire
text_blocks.text: But before he signs what his extension, right? Correct. So, him giving them a trial before he signs an extension, that means he has to be available if he wants an extension, right?

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: I understand that. But hey, today, some guys can go off merit or are going off or are trying to go off merit. I hear you 1000%. But the reality is, that's all I'm saying. Now, I agree, he has to be available. That's all I'm saying. Because when he is available, I mean, he's one of the best. He's one of the best. There's no question. There's no question. So, be available. That's just that simple.

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter and Amar’e Stoudemire debate Wizards' win total
quotes.excerpt: I think they can get into the playoffs or play their way into the playoffs

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: The Wizards are a plus 800 to win 45 games next year. AJ, they drafted, they drafted AD, Young, Trey Young, Trey Johnson. It's three big additions to their team. And I like the kid Koulibaly. Do they make it there? I like Trey Young. Alex Sarr, Trey Johnson as well. Trey Johnson, yes. I agree with you earlier, we talked about the Wizards making the playoffs of some sort. I do think they can, uh, they can get into the playoffs or play their way into the playoffs. So, I'm going to say yes. I, I, I think the Washington Wizards, if healthy, can, can, can get, get, get 45 wins.

text_blocks.speaker: Amar’e Stoudemire
text_blocks.text: So, you going on 45 and saying, yeah. I'm saying they're not winning 45 games. I think they're going to fall short, but they still going to get into the playoffs. I don't think they're going to win 45 games. I just, again, it goes back to that availability. I say 35 games. I just don't know. Um, but I do, I, I, despite them not winning the 45 games, I still think they will get to the play-in or make the playoffs. It doesn't matter about winning the 45 games.

quotes.speaker: Amar’e Stoudemire
quotes.summary_phrase: Amar’e Stoudemire on his high school transition to Lake Wales
quotes.excerpt: I knew I had potential to do something in basketball. I knew I had a chance to hopefully make it to the NBA
quotes.quote: When I was in high school, I was a freshman at Lake Wales High School and I knew I had potential to do something in basketball. I knew I had a chance to hopefully make it to the NBA. At that time, you dream to make it to the NBA. I was 15 years old and I started hanging around the wrong crowd and I was like, no, I'm starting to go down the wrong path. So I went to my coach, Coach Hayes at the time, who was the JV coach, and I said, Coach Hayes, I can't, you know, I got to get out of here Coach Hayes, I can't stick around. Because Lake Wales is a small town and you know what I'm saying? So you got to try to change the environment. And so Coach Hayes said, well, I got two options for you. I got Oak Hill Academy or Mount Zion. So I said, well, what's up with Oak Hill Academy? He said, well, Oak Hill Academy is an all-boys school. Well, I ain't going to that. I ain't going to an all-boys school now. And then he came back and said, well, Mount Zion is what T-Mac went. So I said, well, that's what. That's what I want to go. You know what I'm saying? Because you, because T-Mac, you paid, you paved the way for that, bro. So for me to, for me to, to, to see that you was able to accomplish what you accomplished from high school gave me the inspiration that I can try to do the same thing.

quotes.speaker: Amar’e Stoudemire
quotes.summary_phrase: Amar’e Stoudemire on learning the game of basketball in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: When I got to the NBA, I started learning the game of basketball. I started learning certain plays
quotes.quote: When I was first drafted to Phoenix, you know, I was learning so much, right? Because you know in high school, when you the top player in the country and everything is kind of given to you, the coaching staff and stuff, they let you play. You just do your thing. There's no development, there's no teaching really involved. Just go out there and just dominate, right? So when I got to the NBA, I started learning the game of basketball. I started learning like certain plays and techniques and strategy and movements and these type of things. And so my game started to improve dramatically because I was learning so much. Even throughout Summer League, I went from Summer League to my first NBA game and I improved dramatically in that short period of time because I was starting to learn the game. And throughout my rookie year, I was playing at that time with the point guard Stephon Marbury was my point guard at that time when I first was drafted. And I was just using my athleticism, my quickness and my explosiveness and will. And the game started to become easier, even though my rookie year the game was fast, it was like, damn, everything's happening so fast, but I was still able to apply my dominance as a rookie, my rookie year.

quotes.speaker: Amar’e Stoudemire
quotes.summary_phrase: Amar’e Stoudemire on his toughest defensive matchup
quotes.excerpt: the hardest player for me to guard was Dirk Nowitzki because I wasn't able to get into his bodies
quotes.quote: I mean, we had to play chess, right? Because I'm taking, both kings come off the table, right? So it's, it's me versus whoever the four is. If he get 30, I'm getting 30, right? So we got to, we got to even that match out. And it was, it was tough every night because I would say the hardest player for me to guard was Dirk Nowitzki because I wasn't able to get into his bodies because he kind of flails a little bit. And then that one leg fade away jumper, he's 7-1 and he got that little hitch to throw your your your timing off. Right, and and and so, you know, and he was tough for me to guard. I had to put Shawn Marion on him. I said, Trix, you got him, bro. I can't I can't. Yeah, I I couldn't do nothing with him.

quotes.speaker: Amar’e Stoudemire
quotes.summary_phrase: Amar’e Stoudemire on what drives him to compete
quotes.excerpt: It's the passion. I mean, it had to be something that was dropped down from the heavens, bro
quotes.quote: It's the passion. I mean, it had to be something that was dropped down from the heavens, bro, because long as I can remember, man, since I was a kid, I love basketball. I loved it. You know what I'm saying? I watch it all the time. I watch college basketball. I go to the high school games with my dad. I would dream basketball. I'd keep the ball in my hand everywhere I went. It was just something that I always had, the passion that I always had in me. So when I got to the league, I felt like, you know, you get to the league, you feel like you can do anything. You can jump from outside the paint, you can you can do all this stuff with the basketball. You can score at will. So now that passion is at a higher level now. And and then now you competing against the best and you still being able to to to be in that same category with the best. It's just it's just something about that that passion that continue to drive you every single time.

quotes.speaker: Amar’e Stoudemire
quotes.summary_phrase: Amar’e Stoudemire on his most underrated teammate
quotes.excerpt: I would say Joe Johnson, man. I think I think I think Joe Johnson is underrated
quotes.quote: I would say Joe Johnson, man. I think I think I think Joe Johnson is underrated because Joe at the time, he was our he was our ISO player there, you know what I'm saying? Like when we needed a bucket, we went to Joe. And Joe would create a shot for himself, you know what I'm saying? So we so and that propelled him even all past when he went to Atlanta. You know what I'm saying? So and he became a six-time All-Star and these type of things. But to me, I think his offensive his offensive skill and the way he played the game of basketball is underrated because Joe's a six-time All-Star man and and what he and what he did in his career was special.
